summary: Eugene Jarvis's over-the-top arcade racing series, tracked across Midway arcade releases, Nintendo home ports, handheld spin-offs, and Raw Thrills revivals.

entries.title: Cruis'n USA
entries.definitive_edition: Arcade original plus N64 progression supplement

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / Nintendo 64 emulator for supplement
emulation.notes: Use arcade hardware or preservation for the main run; use N64 emulation only for the secondary unlock loop.

primary.version: Original Midway V Unit arcade release
primary.why: The arcade original is the highest-fidelity and least-compromised version of Cruis'n USA. The Nintendo 64 conversion was downgraded and censored, though it adds home progression features such as saved profiles, paint jobs, and upgrades, so it is only a secondary supplement.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original arcade cabinet or an accurate preservation setup; use the N64/Wii Virtual Console release only for the home progression extras.

secondary.exclusive_content: Home profile saves plus unlockable paint jobs and upgrades
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the N64 progression/unlock loop after the arcade main route.
secondary.why: The home version is lower fidelity and censored but has home-specific progression features.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Midway V Unit arcade release and arcade cabinet baseline.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest fidelity and uncensored original presentation.

all_releases.fidelity: Downgraded and censored home conversion with saved profiles and unlockable upgrades/paint jobs.
all_releases.reason: secondary: home-exclusive progression content, lower fidelity.
skip: same lower-fidelity N64 branch with no separate content advantage.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is the fidelity/authenticity route; N64/Wii VC adds home progression and unlock systems but is downgraded and censored.

entries.remaster_caveats: Wii Virtual Console is the Nintendo 64 version, not the arcade original.

entries.title: Cruis'n World

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / Nintendo 64 emulator for supplement
emulation.notes: Use N64 only for the Moon and Championship content.

primary.why: Cruis'n World began as an arcade release with the series' linked-cabinet presentation and stunt system. The Nintendo 64 port adds a Moon track, Championship mode, unlockables, and four-player split-screen, so arcade remains the primary fidelity route and N64 is the secondary content route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade cabinet/preservation route for the main run, then use the N64 version for the Moon track and Championship mode.

secondary.exclusive_content: Moon track, Championship mode, extra/unlockable home content, and four-player split-screen
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Moon track and Championship mode.
secondary.why: The N64 version is lower fidelity but adds documented home-exclusive content.

all_releases.fidelity: Home port with exclusive Moon track, Championship mode, extra cars/stages, and split-screen.
all_releases.reason: secondary: exclusive home content, lower fidelity than arcade.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is the fidelity route; N64 has extra track/mode content.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern arcade-perfect home release is sourced.

entries.title: Cruis'n Exotica

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / Nintendo 64 emulator / SameBoy or mGBA for GBC
emulation.notes: Use home/handheld versions only for the documented differences.

primary.why: The arcade release is the highest-fidelity version and retains the original licensed-car arcade presentation and PIN system. Nintendo 64 and Game Boy Color are lower-fidelity home/handheld versions with altered content and unlockables, so they are secondary only for preservation sampling.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version for the main run; sample the Nintendo 64 and Game Boy Color versions only for their home/handheld differences.

secondary.exclusive_content: Home-version altered layouts, generic replacement cars, hidden vehicles, and unlockable tracks/cars
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the N64 hidden/unlockable content and changed layouts.
secondary.why: Lower fidelity than arcade but meaningfully different.

secondary.exclusive_content: Handheld reinterpretation with password-based progression and unlockable tracks/cars
secondary.what_to_play: Sample as a handheld demake rather than a full replacement.
secondary.why: It is a distinct portable version, not the fidelity route.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Midway Zeus II arcade release.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest fidelity and original licensed-car presentation.

all_releases.fidelity: Home conversion with altered layouts, replacement cars, and unlockable content.
all_releases.reason: secondary: unique home-version differences and unlockables, lower fidelity.

all_releases.fidelity: Handheld demake with password progression and unlockable tracks/cars.
all_releases.reason: secondary: distinct portable version, not a main-route replacement.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is the fidelity route; N64 and GBC are different home/handheld interpretations with unlockables.

entries.remaster_caveats: Home versions alter content and presentation rather than replacing the arcade original.

entries.title: Cruis'n Velocity

emulation.notes: Use original hardware or accurate GBA emulation.

primary.why: Cruis'n Velocity is a Game Boy Advance-only entry and the only series game not preceded by an arcade release. The GBA release is therefore the complete and only route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Game Boy Advance cartridge on original hardware, Analogue Pocket, or a GBA emulator such as mGBA.

all_releases.fidelity: Only release, with GBA pseudo-3D presentation and link-cable multiplayer.
all_releases.reason: primary: sole platform and complete version.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only the GBA version is sourced.

entries.remaster_caveats: No arcade or modern remaster route is sourced.

entries.title: The Fast and the Furious / Cruis'n
entries.definitive_edition: The Fast and the Furious arcade original

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / Wii hardware or Dolphin for Wii port
emulation.notes: Use the Wii route only for the rebranded home-port artifact.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Raw Thrills arcade cabinet fidelity

primary.version: The Fast and the Furious arcade original
primary.why: The 2007 Wii game titled Cruis'n is a modified home port of Raw Thrills' 2004 arcade game The Fast and the Furious with the film license removed. The arcade original has the stronger cabinet presentation, PIN-based upgrade persistence, and original content context; Wii is lower fidelity and removes the license branding.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Raw Thrills arcade cabinet for the main route; use the Wii Cruis'n release only if preserving the Nintendo-branded home version.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Raw Thrills arcade release with cabinet presentation and PIN-based progression.
all_releases.reason: primary: original and highest-fidelity version of this Cruis'n-adjacent entry.

all_releases.fidelity: Modified Wii home port with film license removed.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity home conversion with no sourced exclusive content advantage.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The arcade original is the stronger and more complete route; the Wii version is a rebranded port.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Wii release is branded Cruis'n because the film license was removed; do not conflate it with the 1990s arcade trilogy.

entries.title: Cruis'n Blast

emulation.notes: Use Switch for the complete home version; use the cabinet for arcade controls.

primary.why: Cruis'n Blast began in arcades, but the Nintendo Switch version adds additional modes, cars, and tracks, making it the most complete home route while retaining the modern Raw Thrills style.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Nintendo Switch version; use the arcade cabinet only for the original cabinet experience.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Raw Thrills arcade cabinet release.
all_releases.reason: skip: authentic cabinet route, but Switch adds more modes, cars, and tracks.

all_releases.fidelity: Enhanced home release with additional modes, cars, and tracks.
all_releases.reason: primary: most complete release of Cruis'n Blast.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade has the cabinet experience; Switch is more complete with expanded home content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Switch is expanded from the arcade original rather than an arcade-perfect cabinet replacement.
